notes: PSA 13.2 ng/mL. PI-RADS 4. PSAD 0.14. Prostate volume 96 mL. DRE nodus. csPCa 0.64.

note_sections.t: Re-evaluation for rising PSA and progression of known ISUP GG2 prostate cancer to determine definitive treatment strategy.

Recently retired civil engineer with a history of type 2 diabetes and hypercholesterolaemia, currently managed with metformin and atorvastatin. He reports mild lower urinary tract symptoms with an IPSS score of 7. The patient lives alone but maintains a close relationship with his unmarried partner, who acts as his primary contact. He remains physically active, enjoying hiking on weekends, and consumes approximately 17 units of alcohol weekly. He is a former smoker with a 23 pack-year history, having quit in 2023. His PSA trajectory has been volatile, dropping to 2.5 ng/mL in May 2024 before rebounding to 6.4 ng/mL in September and surging to 13.2 ng/mL in February 2025. He reports no bone pain, haematuria, or systemic symptoms.

Per rectum, a distinct nodular area is palpable in the mid-left peripheral zone, consistent with a cT2a clinical stage. The prostate is enlarged but otherwise smooth. General examination is unremarkable with stable vital signs and no signs of peripheral lymphadenopathy or bony tenderness.

admin: Patient self-employed; flexible appointment slots requested.
